Tecendo Redes surgiu de uma parceria com:
Tecendo Redes grew out of a partnership with fishing associations on the Ceará coast. The program offers training in mobile photography, video production, podcasting and social media management — tools for communities to tell their own stories.

Over four months, young people aged 16 to 25 produced a podcast about life in small-scale fishing, a short documentary about traditional net-weaving techniques and a collective social media profile that already has more than 3,000 followers.

The project teaches technology as a language — a way to carry people's voices further.

O Laboratório Passarinho nasceu de uma p:
Laboratório Passarinho began with a simple question: what happens when you give a group of children scissors, glue and scrap materials and ask them to invent a sound?

Over six weeks, thirty young people aged 8 to 14 built instruments from plastic bottles, cans, rubber bands and bamboo. Each instrument gained a name, a story and its own repertoire. The process culminated in a presentation open to the neighborhood — a chance to share what had been learned and invented.

The lab showed that music can be a starting point for creative autonomy: those who make the instrument choose the sound; those who choose the sound begin to hear the world differently.

Cartografias do Possível foi uma residên:
Cartografias do Possível was an artistic residency held on a rural property near Atibaia in March and April 2024. Six artists from different disciplines — visual arts, music, photography and writing — lived and worked together for eight weeks.

The project began with a question: how does a place speak? And how do we learn to listen?

Each resident developed an original work from the immersive experience: walks, conversations with local residents and recordings of the forest, rain and animals. The process resulted in a collective publication and a traveling exhibition shown in three cities.

Um livro infantil criado a partir da esc: A children’s book shaped by listening to children, exploring mangroves, the city and the right to belong. A Sabichinho project in Santa Catarina, rooted in Florianópolis.
Quem tem direito a habitar a cidade?: Who has the right to inhabit the city?

A capybara. A mangrove. A letter.
A protagonista vive em um mangue que dev: The protagonist lives in a mangrove that was supposed to become a park. When she discovers that this promise has been left behind and her home is under threat, she decides to act: bring other voices together and write a letter to the mayor.
Na narrativa em construção, a capivara e: In the developing story, the capybara meets children, a traditional healer, a fisher and other inhabitants of the mangrove. A crab, an egret, a mullet and a broad-snouted caiman help tell the story of a place where nature, memory and community life meet.
O livro abre uma conversa sobre pertenci: The book opens a conversation about belonging, environmental commitments and collective action. One question runs through the story: what can we do together to care for the place where we live?
Florianópolis é o território de referênc: Florianópolis is the project’s reference territory: a city where mangroves, neighborhoods, waterways and buildings share the same space. The literary project starts with this coexistence and with debates about how the city grows and cares for its environments.
O debate em torno do Parque do Jacaré ap: The debate surrounding Parque do Jacaré appears in the project materials as one of the inspirations for the promise of a park in the story. The mangrove enters the book as a habitat for many animals and a place of work, knowledge, memories and human connections.
A criação se conecta também a outras cid: The creative process also connects with other cities in Santa Catarina. The experiences of children and educators broaden the understanding of place while keeping Florianópolis as its starting point.
O processo da Sabichinho começa pela esc: Sabichinho’s process begins with listening. In workshops, children invent characters, draw, tell stories and talk about the places where they live. These materials inform the book’s narrative and visual choices.
Cada participante pode criar uma capivar: Each participant can create a capybara or another inhabitant of the same environment, with a name, personality, dreams and a particular way of seeing the world. Imagination connects the story’s conflict with each child’s own experiences.
As cartas e os cartazes são parte centra: Letters and posters are central to this process: the characters describe who they are, what is happening in their territory and what they would like to change. The methodology includes sending the letters to public authorities, bringing literature and civic participation together.
A book to create and share.
O projeto está em desenvolvimento. A pro: The project is in development. The proposal includes a 48-page illustrated book, an initial print run of 2,000 copies for free distribution and five creative listening workshops with children and educators in Santa Catarina.
Também estão previstas uma edição digita: Plans also include a digital edition under a Creative Commons license, accessibility resources such as an audiobook and VLibras, public launches and distribution through schools, libraries and cultural spaces.
A construção editorial reúne os materiai: The editorial process brings workshop materials together through collective writing, illustration and editing. The quantities and formats presented here are project goals; they do not represent completed deliveries.
